checkpoint_review: The Router was generally accurate but slightly lenient on the 'Eyes' checkpoint. While it marked 'gold-flecked irises' as false due to resolution, the eye region also shows low structural definition typical of AI smoothing, not just lighting issues. The Router correctly identified the limb digit ambiguity as a failure point. The 'Head shape' and 'Coloration' checkpoints are correctly marked as present. The Router's assessment of the tail is valid.
artifact_review: The Router underestimated the severity of the text artifact. The Image Text Auditor revealed the text is 'inaCy.' with low confidence (0.50), confirming it is gibberish/hallucinated watermarking, which is a distinct AI artifact (Severity 3.0). The Router noted limb fusion (Severity 2.5); the Animal Pose Auditor supports this with a HIGH risk level (47% low-confidence keypoints), particularly in the face and limbs. This confirms structural softness/fusion. The Topology Auditor's high mask score (0.95) only confirms the object is segmented, not that the boundary is sharp; visual inspection confirms slight bleeding into the dark background. New finding: The Pose Auditor's failure on facial keypoints (Nose/Eyes < 0.3 confidence) indicates the head structure is geometrically ambiguous, reinforcing the 'melting' artifact diagnosis.
alignment_reasoning: The Fine Grained Classifier strongly confirms the class (Logit 7.96 vs 5.02 for next best), indicating high semantic alignment. Major features (color pattern, body shape, parotoid glands) are visually present and correct. However, the failure to render distinct digits and the lack of fine iris detail prevent a perfect score. The image is clearly a salamander, but lacks the micro-anatomical precision of a high-quality macro photograph.
artifact_reasoning: Multiple artifacts detected. 1) Structural/Limb Fusion: Confirmed by Router visual inspection and Pose Auditor's HIGH risk (low confidence on limbs/face). Digits are indistinct/melted. 2) Text Gibberish: Confirmed by OCR as 'inaCy.', a hallucinated watermark. 3) Edge Bleeding: Slight softness at the black-skin/dark-rock interface. These issues compound to lower the artifact score significantly below the reference 'high' quality images.
